label: binary interaction phrase
explanation: It fires on tokens in local phrases where two entities are combined, mixed, connected, or otherwise interacted, especially the short function word that links them (with, to, and, by, from, on, of) and sometimes the nearby items. It fires most strongly when the two-item relation is explicit and central, particularly "with" in X-with-Y or X-to-Y technical/scientific contexts, and more weakly on less central content words. It stays silent on ordinary function words and most tokens outside such two-item relational constructions, including the first token.
